memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You will not surely die," the serpent said to the woman. "For God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil." — Gen 3:4–5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having planted doubt, the serpent now moves to open contradiction. Where God said "you will surely die," he says flatly, "You will not surely die." The quiet question has become a bold lie.

But notice the deeper poison in his words. He suggests that God is keeping something good back from Adam and Eve — that God is not really for them, but against them. "You will be like God," he promises, as though the Creator were a rival to be envied rather than a Father to be trusted. He paints God as small and stingy, and makes rebellion look like freedom.

This is the lie underneath so many of our own temptations. We are tempted to believe that God is withholding, that His "no" is meant to rob us of joy, and that we would be better off deciding good and evil for ourselves. Sin always promises more than it can give.

Dear friend, the wonderful truth is that we do not have to grasp at being like God, because God came down to us. The One who was truly equal with God did not cling to it, but humbled Himself for our sake (Phil 2:6–8). Where Adam reached up and fell, Christ stooped down and saved. That is the God we can trust completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to believe God is withholding something good from you?
2. How does the humility of Jesus change the way you see God's heart toward you?
3. What "no" from God can you learn to trust as an expression of His love?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have believed the lie that You are against me. Thank You that in Jesus You came down to save me, proving Your love beyond all doubt. Help me to trust Your heart even when I don't understand Your commands. Amen.
